audit.whatIsWrong: Two strings sell the early lane as a free poke war: 'poke Locke off the wave from a range he cannot answer' and 'Q Winds of War out-ranges his walk-up'.
audit.why: Ritual Nails is thrown from 950. Winds of War casts at 825. Locke out-ranges Galio's only ranged tool, so a poke war is the one pattern Galio must not pick.
audit.corrected: Lane stays favoured (53.63% over 1641 games) but the reason is trade windows, not range — rewritten in spikes[0], whys[1] and phases[0].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 and late spikes were generic ('Magic Pen spike', 'stacked MR'), and the late text calls Hero's Entrance global.
audit.why: Hero's Entrance is 180/160/140 at range 4000/4750/5500 and must be cast onto an ALLY — not global. Locke's real 6 spike is Purgatory at 120s plus Silver Stake, whose on-hit magic damage grows with the target's MISSING health.
audit.corrected: Spikes now name Purgatory's 120s and the missing-health scaling; the global claim is removed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in either layer states what Soul Ignition does to your damage.
audit.why: Riot: Soul Ignition makes Locke 'heal back a portion of the damage he takes during the effect'. Damage poured into an ignited Locke is partly refunded to him at the end of the duration, and the ability is 18/17/16/15/14.
audit.corrected: Hold Winds of War and the taunt until Soul Ignition ends, or land Grievous Wounds before the refund resolves. Written into early, trading, report[5] and loading.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns says Ashen Pursuit 'resets on takedowns'.
audit.why: The kit's autoReset flag on Ashen Pursuit means an AUTO-ATTACK reset, and Riot's description is 'teleports to a location before dashing to attack his next target'. Nothing in the kit supports a takedown cooldown reset. Cooldown is a flat 10s at every rank.
audit.corrected: Reframed as an attack reset — the teleport is the tell, the auto is the damage — with the flat 10s stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization says 'Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal.'
audit.why: Grievous Wounds reduces healing regardless of its source, and Soul Ignition's refund is healing. The refund resolves at the END of the duration, which makes the timing, not the purchase, the real decision.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds is not optional; apply it before Soul Ignition expires.

audit.whatIsWrong: No real cooldown numbers anywhere despite the whole page being built around 'the post-E window'.
audit.why: Ritual Nails 10/9/8/7/6, Ashen Pursuit a flat 10s, Soul Ignition 18/17/16/15/14, Purgatory 120/100/80.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and loading.

edits.before: Q Winds of War online — poke Locke off the wave from a range he cannot answer.
edits.after: Ritual Nails reaches 950 to your 825 — you do not win the poke war, so trade.

edits.before: Level 2 stays Galio: Q Winds of War out-ranges his walk-up, so you poke him off the wave for free.
edits.after: Level 2 stays Galio, but not on range — his Ritual Nails throws 950 to your 825, so trade rather than poke.

edits.before: Constant Q poke, W held for his combo
edits.after: Hold damage while Soul Ignition burns

edits.before: MR stacking to blank his burst

Levels 1-5 are simply yours: W Shield of Durand plus your Colossal Smash passive blunt everything Locke's magic chip does, and Q Winds of War pokes him from a range he cannot answer. Shove and harass freely — his only prayer is catching you with W on cooldown, so trade around its uptime and build a CS lead while he watches.
edits.after: Levels 1-5 are simply yours, but not because you out-range him — Ritual Nails throws 950 to Winds of War's 825. You win on damage timing: Soul Ignition (W, 18s at rank 1) refunds a portion of the damage he TAKES while it burns, so everything you pour into an ignited Locke comes partly back. Hold Q and the taunt until it expires, then trade and shove.

edits.before: From level 6 through first item the lane goes even — his R Purgatory executes you below threshold and his Magic Pen spike makes one catch lethal. Stay above half HP, keep W in your pocket for his engage, and start using your own R to cash the early lead on other lanes instead of coin-flipping trades here.
edits.after: From level 6 through first item the lane goes even — Purgatory (120s) executes you below threshold and Silver Stake's on-hit magic damage grows with the health you are MISSING, so a chipped Galio dies to his autos alone. Stay topped up, keep W for Ashen Pursuit, and spend your own R on other lanes rather than coin-flipping here.

edits.before: At two-plus items the matchup is Galio's again: stacked MR turns his single-target burst into chip damage while your taunt and global R decide teamfights. Force grouped fights, flank-taunt onto his carries, and never let him find a free pick on your backline — deny the catch and he has no way back into the game.
edits.after: At two-plus items the matchup is Galio's again: stacked MR turns his burst into chip while your taunt and Hero's Entrance decide fights — cast it on an ally within 4000 units, it is not global. Force grouped fights, flank-taunt onto his carries, and never let him find a free pick on your backline — deny the catch and he has no way back.

edits.before: Level 6 flattens to even — R Purgatory can execute a low Galio even through your W, so stop coin-flipping trades at half HP.
edits.after: Level 6 flattens to even — Purgatory executes a low Galio, and Silver Stake's on-hit grows with the health you are missing.

edits.before: Magic Pen spike means one catch converts — track his engage range and stay topped up.
edits.after: Silver Stake scales with your MISSING health — one catch converts, so stay topped up.

edits.before: 2+ items swings back to Galio — your MR wall and global R outscale his single-target burst completely.
edits.after: 2+ items swings back to Galio — your MR wall and a 4000-range Hero's Entrance outscale his single-target burst.

edits.before: - Locke Ritual Nails (Marks): matchup-defining — The nail marks are his whole engine — without 2-3 stacks on you his blink-in barely dents; sidestep the recasts and punish the ten seconds of nothing. Track it before every step-up. - Locke E (Ashen Pursuit): his ONLY mobility, resets on takedowns — the post-E window is the lane. - Locke R (Purgatory): never fight at sliver HP inside the zone.
edits.after: - Ritual Nails: 10s at rank 1, 6s maxed, thrown from 950 — further than your 825, so sidestep the recasts instead of trading poke. - Ashen Pursuit: a flat 10s at every rank and his only exit; it is an ATTACK reset, so the teleport is the tell and the auto is the damage. - Soul Ignition: 18s, and it refunds damage he takes. - Purgatory: 120s at rank 1, 80s maxed.

edits.before: Early HP and MR blunt the nail chip (his damage is AP). A stopwatch/Zhonya’s-class answer beats Purgatory outright: untargetable at the floor = execute denied. Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal.
edits.after: Early HP and MR blunt the nail chip (his damage is AP). A Zhonya's-class answer beats Purgatory: untargetable at the floor = execute denied. Grievous Wounds is NOT optional — Soul Ignition refunds at the end of its duration, so land it before then.

edits.before: Good trade: His Q recasts whiffed and E is spent — take the trade your kit is built for. Bad trade: Fighting with 2-3 nail marks on you while his E is up — that’s his entire kill script, pre-paid.
edits.after: Good trade: his Q recasts whiffed and Ashen Pursuit is spent — a flat 10 seconds with no exit. Bad trade: dumping Winds of War and the taunt into a burning Soul Ignition, which hands him back a slice of all of it.

edits.before: The nail marks are his whole engine — without 2-3 stacks on you his blink-in barely dents; sidestep the recasts and punish the ten seconds of nothing. Only commit once it is down or baited.
edits.after: The nail marks are his whole engine — without 2-3 stacks on you his blink-in barely dents. Ashen Pursuit is a flat 10s at every rank, so a spent blink is ten seconds with no exit.

edits.before: Track Locke’s Ritual Nails (Marks): The nail marks are his whole engine — without 2-3 stacks on you his blink-in barely dents; sidestep the recasts and punish the ten seconds of nothing. Commit only while it is down.
edits.after: Soul Ignition refunds a portion of the damage he TAKES while it burns — hold Winds of War and the taunt until it ends. Ashen Pursuit is an attack reset: the teleport is the tell, the auto is the damage.

edits.before: - Galio vs Locke - Track: Locke Ritual Nails (Marks). - Watch your own mark stacks like a cooldown. - Engage only on the post-E window. - Never fight at sliver HP inside Purgatory.
edits.after: - Galio vs Locke - Do not feed Soul Ignition: it refunds damage he takes. - His nails throw 950, your Q 825. - Engage on the spent 10s blink. - Stay above the Purgatory floor.

edits.before: Level 1 he’s a 125-range mana champ throwing nails — step off the recast lines and take what the range difference offers.
edits.after: Level 1 he is a mana champ throwing nails from 950 — further than your 825, so step off the recast lines and last-hit.

notes: Largest sample in the slice (1641 games) and it carried a load-bearing range error: both layers told the Galio player to win a poke war, but Ritual Nails is 950 and Winds of War is 825. Second: Soul Ignition refunds a portion of the damage Locke TAKES during it, which inverts the natural instinct to burn your kit into a champion who just lit himself on fire — that interaction appeared nowhere. Third: breakdown.cooldowns claimed Ashen Pursuit 'resets on takedowns'; the kit's autoReset flag is an auto-attack reset and the cooldown is a flat 10s at every rank. UNVERIFIED and deliberately not written: the kit derives a 'grounding' flag on Purgatory, which if real would deny Justice Punch inside the zone. Riot's text only says 'binding artifact', so I left it out rather than assert it. Also unverified: phases[0].why and two breakdown strings describe Locke as '125 range' — the kit library carries no attack range, so I did not touch that claim.
